terra.problem: Saying nobody can claim they weren't warned implies everyone received the warning. The text directs Moses to deliver it to Pharaoh.
It reveals the later locust plague in an ongoing story.
The text says there will be no swarms in Goshen, not that the LORD's people have a quiet day.
The text says no swarms will be found in Goshen, not that there will be no flies at all. It also says the LORD's people live there, not that the land belongs to them.
Saying flies are everywhere except Goshen overstates the text: it says no swarms will be found there.
The passage doesn't say that nobody is hiding; it simply doesn't give hiding as the reason.
Goshen being in Egypt doesn't establish that it isn't a three-day walk. The text gives no travel time to Goshen.
Exodus 8:20 calls it the water; it doesn't identify it as the Nile.
Pharaoh doesn't tell them to take their time walking. That adds permission he doesn't give.
The text sets the time as tomorrow but doesn't say Pharaoh received a day's notice of that timing.
Pharaoh sent officials and found out the result; the text doesn't say he saw it for himself.
Saying Pharaoh wasn't ready to say yes assigns him an unstated feeling or reason.
The text says the soot will become fine dust over the land, not that it comes down everywhere.
The text doesn't say the dust settles everywhere.
“No jokes from me here” comments on how Papa is telling the passage.
Saying the fine dust brings the boils adds a causal connection the text doesn't state.
The claim that Pharaoh's magicians tried to match Moses earlier needs a reference outside this passage.
